questions.question: You need exactly 500 uniformly chosen transactions from a stream whose total length is unknown until it ends, using little memory. Which approach has the right shape?
options: Keep each item with probability 500 / (yesterday's count) as it passes
Keep the first 500 items and stop reading
Keep a 500-slot reservoir; item n replaces a random slot with probability 500 / n
Buffer everything, shuffle at the end, take the first 500
questions.explanation: Reservoir sampling gives exactly k items, uniformly, in O(k) memory without knowing n in advance. A fixed probability gives a variable count and depends on a guess; the first 500 is a time-of-day sample; buffering everything is correct but needs O(n) memory, which is the problem being avoided.

questions.question: After n items, reservoir sampling with k slots guarantees each item seen so far is in the reservoir with what probability?
options: k / n
k / (n - k)
questions.explanation: The induction: item n enters with probability k/n, and each earlier item (there with probability k/(n-1)) survives unless item n enters and picks its slot, probability 1/n, giving k/(n-1) * (n-1)/n = k/n. 1/n would be the probability for a one-slot reservoir.

questions.question: Shuffling [a, b, c] by swapping each position with a uniformly random position in the whole list is biased. What is the arithmetic reason?
options: Swapping a position with itself is wasted work that skews later swaps
The 27 equally likely execution paths cannot divide evenly among 6 permutations
The random index must be drawn from a cryptographic generator to be uniform
Three elements are too few for any shuffle to be uniform
questions.explanation: n^n = 27 paths map onto n! = 6 permutations, and 27 is not a multiple of 6, so some permutations get 5 paths and others 4. Fisher-Yates has exactly n! paths, one per permutation. Self-swaps are fine; Fisher-Yates allows them too.

questions.question: Randomized quickselect is a Las Vegas algorithm. What does that mean here?
options: It returns the exact k-th smallest every time; only the running time varies with the random pivots
It returns an approximately correct rank with probability at least 3/4
It runs in guaranteed O(n) time but may return a wrong element with small probability
It uses a random seed derived from the system clock so results differ between runs
questions.explanation: Las Vegas: correctness is certain, time is random (expected O(n), worst O(n^2) with vanishing probability). The third option describes a Monte Carlo algorithm. The result does not differ between runs; the test asserts the same answer under twenty seeds.

questions.question: Miller-Rabin with 10 random bases reports 561 as composite and 1,000,003 as probably prime. Which statement about its errors is correct?
options: Both answers could be wrong with probability at most 4^-10
The prime verdict is certain; the composite verdict is wrong with probability at most 4^-10
Neither verdict is certain, which is why 561 is called a Carmichael number
The composite verdict is certain; the prime verdict is wrong with probability at most 4^-10
questions.explanation: A witness is a proof of compositeness, so 'composite' is never wrong. 'Probably prime' means no witness was found in 10 tries, which a composite survives with probability at most 4^-10. 561 is a Carmichael number because it fools the plain Fermat test, not Miller-Rabin.

questions.question: An auditor asks you to prove that today's 500-transaction sample was not hand-picked. What property of the sampler makes that possible, and what would make it unsafe elsewhere?
options: A cryptographic generator, which makes the sample unpredictable to everyone but also impossible to reproduce for the auditor
Sampling the first 500 items of the stream, which anyone can verify from the recorded stream order without any generator
Reducing nextLong() modulo n for each draw, which spreads the sample evenly across the whole day's stream
A recorded seed for a deterministic generator, which makes the sample reproducible but predictable to anyone holding the seed
questions.explanation: Given the seed and the stream, the auditor regenerates the identical sample, proving it was not chosen by hand. The same predictability is why a seeded non-cryptographic generator must never produce tokens or keys. First-500 is reproducible but not uniform; modulo reduction is biased for most n.
